spec.name: Almoravid Koubba
spec.description: The Almoravid Koubba is one of the oldest surviving monuments in Marrakech and a rare example of Almoravid architecture. Built in the early 12th century during the reign of Ali ibn Yusuf, it was probably part of the original Ben Youssef Mosque complex and served as a pavilion for ritual ablutions. The monument is especially notable for its carved dome, geometric and vegetal decoration, Arabic inscriptions and early examples of muqarnas ornamentation.

access.comment: Free entry is available to Moroccan nationals every Friday and on the first day of national and religious holidays. Admission conditions and prices may change.

timeline.title: Construction during the Almoravid period
timeline.description: The Koubba was built during the reign of the Almoravid ruler Ali ibn Yusuf, probably as part of the nearby Ben Youssef Mosque complex.

timeline.title: Almohad conquest of Marrakech
timeline.description: The Almohads conquered Marrakech and many Almoravid religious buildings were destroyed or substantially altered. The Koubba survived.

timeline.title: Rediscovery documented
timeline.description: The existence of the buried monument was documented by scholars after centuries of accumulated construction and rising ground levels had concealed much of the structure.

timeline.title: Archaeological excavation
timeline.description: Archaeological investigations uncovered the monument and surrounding remains, including water installations associated with its original function.
